overview: White fianchettoes against the Pirc with 4.g3 and Bg2, followed by Nge2 or Nf3, O-O and a quiet build-up. Black replies with ...Bg7, ...c6 or ...O-O and counters with ...e5 or ...c5. The game is slow and strategic with White's centre cramping Black, but Black has solid, flexible counterplay.

white_ideas.idea: Play Bg2, Nge2 or Nf3, O-O and Be3
Keep the e4-d4 centre supported by the fianchetto
Push e5 or advance in the centre when Black commits

black_ideas.idea: Break with ...c5 or ...e5 to hit the centre
Trade pieces and use the fianchetto bishop on g7

typical_structures.structure: White e4-d4 centre with g3 fianchetto against the Pirc g7 bishop

character.notes: The fianchetto set-up is slow and avoids the forcing Austrian-type attacks.

soundness.notes: A solid line for both sides.

structure.notes: The centre stays in tension until Black breaks with ...e5 or ...c5.

approach.notes: A recognised quiet line against the Pirc and Modern, played by strong players.

level.notes: Plans are strategic and clear and there is little to memorise.
